Subject: MAP kickoff: performance benchmarking & target close

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday — the team and I are excited about Redwood as the serving layer for our semantic search and summarization endpoints. As we discussed, Procurement needs a clear MAP with objective benchmarking criteria so we can sign off before end of month.

Can you share a short benchmarking plan that lays out: workload profile (prompt lengths, token mix), concurrency targets, TTFT expectations, and pass/fail criteria? We also want to know what you need from our side (sample prompts, dataset slices, network egress constraints).

Attached is a short MAP draft the business team pulled together (nimbus_map_initial.pdf). Ideally we run a final performance sweep during the week of Aug 24 so results can be reviewed in the closing committee on Aug 28.

Best,

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: performance benchmarking & target close

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear asks and the draft MAP. I reviewed the PDF and sketched a concise benchmarking plan you can include in your MAP. I attached a spreadsheet (tessa-nimbus-map-v1.xlsx) that breaks the plan into phases (lab validation, controlled load, and production shadow). Below is the executive summary and pass/fail criteria so Procurement has concrete SLOs.

Executive summary (quick):
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference economics and latency under representative Nimbus queries to meet contract SLAs and go/no-go before Aug 28 close.
- Scope: two endpoints — semantic-search (rerank + embed+search pipeline) and summarization (single-turn long-context).
- Phases: 1) Lab (functionality + baseline latency) 2) Load (throughput & concurrency) 3) Regression & quality check (prompt set).

Workload definition (representative):
- Semantic-search: 40% of traffic; avg prompt tokens = 64; response tokens = 128; typical concurrency target = 150 concurrent requests across a pool of 6 GPUs.
- Summarization: 60% of traffic; avg prompt tokens = 512; response tokens = 256; concurrency target = 40 concurrent requests across same cluster.
- Mixed burst profile: 30s spikes simulated every 5 minutes to emulate peak usage.

Key metrics to capture:
- Latency: TTFT (time-to-first-token) and P50/P95/P99 generation latency per endpoint and per token-length bucket.
- Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec sustained at target concurrency.
- Resource utilization: GPU % utilization, memory, and KV-cache hit ratio.
- Error rates: exact HTTP error distribution and token generation failures.

SLOs / Success criteria (pass = all met):
- Summarization TTFT P95 <= 350 ms (for 512 prompt / 256 response)
- Semantic-search end-to-end P95 latency <= 250 ms
- Sustained throughput: sustain 3.5k requests/min with <1% error rate across both endpoints
- Concurrency handling: no more than 10% P95 latency degradation at 20% above target concurrency
- Quality regression: BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity regression <= 1.5% vs baseline eval set

Test harness considerations (what we need from Nimbus):
- A 3k-item prompt set with representative tokens per endpoint (we can work from sanitized slices of your production traffic)
- Dataset of 200 golden outputs for quality regression
- Network egress constraints or private VPC test access if you want shadow runs on your environment

Timing & owner recommendations:
- Aug 11–14: lab validation (Redwood infra team — Marissa leads)
- Aug 17–21: controlled load tests (Redwood infra + Nimbus test account — Karthik leads load harness)
- Aug 24–25: production-shadow sweep (joint run)
- Aug 26–27: results analysis and executive summary (Tessa / Marissa)

Next steps: If that looks reasonable, can Nimbus confirm the prompt set availability and a preferred window during Aug 24–25 for the final sweep? I can book time with our infra test cluster now.

Thanks — attaching the detailed plan as a spreadsheet.

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-1212

Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: FW: MAP kickoff: performance benchmarking & target close

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Alicia's note and the plan I returned. Quick alignment items before we commit the infra run: 

1) Test cluster sizing: for the target concurrency (150 semantic-search + 40 summarization), I'm proposing an initial cluster of 6x A100-80GB equiv instances with auto-burst to 8 nodes for spikes. Can you validate that this gives us the KV-cache hit ratios we expect and won't OOM on 512-token contexts?

2) Harness & load profile: Karthik, can you reuse the cluster-harness from the Stellar PoC or do we need new load generators to emulate the 30s spike profile? Also confirm how we will measure TTFT precisely (server-side timestamp vs client-side).

3) Quality checks: Marissa, please own the regression pass — we'll need the 200 golden outputs and the scripts to compute semantic-similarity and ROUGE. If anything looks off beyond 1.5% regression we escalate to model lead.

I'll block tentative windows on Aug 17 and Aug 24 for internal test prep and the joint sweep. Sergio, FYI on customer exec ask for Aug 28 close — might need an on-call for results review.

Thanks — keep replies short so I can coordinate with Alicia and Procurement.

— Tessa

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@nimbusanalytics.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: performance benchmarking & target close

Tessa / team — this looks good and thanks for the detailed plan. Procurement confirmed the MAP structure and the Aug 24 window works for our infra team. A few quick items:

- We'll deliver the 3k prompt set (sanitized) by Aug 20 and the 200 golden outputs the same day.
- Procurement attached a short security questionnaire you'll see in this thread (nimbus-security-questionnaire.pdf) — legal wants the answers before close.
- Can Redwood confirm whether the P95 TTFT numbers above account for TLS termination and VPC egress hops? We prefer numbers that reflect our production topology.

We'll plan to run the joint final sweep Aug 24–25 (we'll join the first few hours). If results meet the SLOs you listed, we can push for an Aug 28 close. Please confirm a single Slack/Zoom bridge for the run and who will be the point on Redwood side.

Appreciate the fast turn-around — looking forward to the runs.

Best,
Alicia
